comparison: Both evaluate TE expression patterns in thymic cells (C3, C32-C37). OpenEval finds the hierarchical clustering and statistical enrichment tests support the claims. Peer reviewers praise the single-cell analysis and diversity findings without raising concerns. Both support these descriptive findings, though peer review also includes methodology claims (C115-C117) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Both address TF-TE interaction analysis (C4, C6, C39-C48, C114). OpenEval finds the methodology sound with appropriate validation and accepts the low correlation threshold as validated through bootstrap. Peer reviewer questions the biological significance of the NK cell example (ETS1/PRF1/KLRD1), finding it 'abrupt and unconnected' to thymic function despite accepting the data. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to relevance concerns.

Both evaluate Shannon entropy analysis and mosaic vs. homogeneous TE expression patterns (C5, C49-C60, C97). OpenEval finds the statistical methods appropriate and the mosaic/homogeneous distinction well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as a key finding showing diversity in thymic antigen-presenting cells. Both rate SUPPORTED with no disagreements.

Both address dsRNA detection and proposed link to IFN secretion (C9-C10, C61-C67, C107-C108). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting J2 antibody data is solid but the mechanistic link to IFN secretion lacks functional validation. Peer reviewer also rates UNCERTAIN, stating 'evidence is totally too weak' and noting only correlation, not causation. Both agree the causal claim is speculative despite accepting the dsRNA detection data.

Both evaluate knockout mouse analysis showing non-redundant regulation by Aire, Fezf2, and Chd4 (C8, C68-C82). OpenEval finds the differential expression analysis uses appropriate statistical methods with stringent thresholds and proper validation. Peer reviewer identifies this as an 'interesting finding' with no specific concerns raised. Both rate SUPPORTED.

Both address MS identification of TE-derived MAPs (C7, C83-C87). OpenEval acknowledges the low number of identified peptides but finds the approach sound and the sensitivity limitation reasonable. Peer reviewer views the MS validation positively, calling it 'worthwhile' despite limited numbers. Both rate SUPPORTED, accepting the technical limitations while valuing the direct evidence.

Both address speculative proposals about TE role in autoimmunity prevention (C11, C102-C103, C108, C111). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is logical but requires functional validation. Peer reviewer also rates UNCERTAIN, noting 'overstatements' and recommending 'more caution' in conclusions. Both agree the proposals are reasonable but not definitively supported by the data.

OpenEval R8 evaluates background/established facts (C1-C2, C25-C31) as SUPPORTED context. Peer R1 includes some of these claims (C2, C28) alongside primary findings. Both agree these are accurate representations of established knowledge, though they group them differently with other claims.

OpenEval evaluates established thymic biology background (C12-C24) as SUPPORTED context from literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these background claims were not specifically addressed in peer reviews.

OpenEval R10 evaluates contextual claims from literature (C88-C113) as SUPPORTED background. Peer R6 includes some overlapping claims (C29, C101-C102) but focuses on MS validation findings. Both treat these as accurate context rather than primary findings.

OpenEval R11 evaluates methodology descriptions (C115-C117) as SUPPORTED and appropriate. Peer R1 includes these methodology claims alongside primary findings about TE expression patterns. Both agree the methodological approach is sound.

OpenEval R1 includes negative correlation with proliferation (C38) as part of broader TE expression analysis, rating it SUPPORTED. Peer R7 specifically questions this correlation (C38, C91), with reviewer asking for more explanation. Authors provided speculative interpretation about senescent cells that reviewer accepted cautiously. Represents different emphasis on same finding.
